description: (0.5.0, Draft) The Agent Card pointer https://acdp.io/ext/a2a/v1 and the identity binding to AITP (RFC-ACDP-0022 §3.1, §9).

input.note: Use the a2a-001 Card extensions (AITP entry and ACDP entry) and body.

expected.behavior: The Card carries exactly one AgentExtension with uri https://acdp.io/ext/a2a/v1, required false, params {registry, agentId}; agentId equals every published body's agent_id.
A Card whose params.agentId names another DID (e.g. did:key:z6MkhaXgBZDvotDkL5257faiztiGiC2QtKLGpbnnEGta2doK) fails §8 step 2 for the a2a-001 body, even though the body's signature verifies.

With the AITP entry params.aid = aid:pubkey:O2onvM62pC1io6jQKm8Nc2UyFXcd4kOmOsBIoYtZ2ik, the did:key agent_id encodes the same Ed25519 key and the binding holds; the tagged form aid:pubkey:ed25519:<same> also holds; an AID for any other key fails the binding.
Both the AITP and the ACDP extensions on one Card are accepted; neither URI is mistaken for the other (byte comparison).
Two ACDP entries, or params missing agentId, give the holder no pointer: it proceeds as if the Card had none and relies only on its own trust configuration.
An agent MUST NOT mark the extension required; a holder ignores required when deciding trust.

scenarios.name: G — untrusted pointer and fetch rules (holder)

expected.behavior: A params.registry outside the holder's allowlist, or resolving to a private, loopback or link-local address, is not fetched (RFC-ACDP-0006 §7, RFC-ACDP-0008 §4.8–§4.9); a link naming a registry other than params.registry is not by itself a failure.
